summary: Jack Kornfield is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Dartmouth College under Wing-tsit Chan, with Ajahn Chah, Mahasi Sayadaw, and Dipa Ma, and earned a PhD from Saybrook University. He co-founded Spirit Rock Meditation Center.
Jack Laughlin is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999 and held an academic post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Ensink was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and served on the faculty at the University of Groningen starting in 1954, first as lecturer and later professor.

Jacob Grimm was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the University of Marburg from around 1802 to 1805. He later held posts at the University of Göttingen (circa 1830–1837) and Frederick William University Berlin (1841).
Jacob Holubeck is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2013.

Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held academic posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at the College of William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Neusner was a religious studies scholar educated at Harvard, Oxford, Columbia, and the Jewish Theological Seminary. He held positions at UW–Milwaukee, Brandeis, the University of South Florida (1990–2003), and Bard College (~1994–2014).

Jacob P. Dalton is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez Jr. He held posts at Yale and the University of California, Berkeley, including an endowed professorship.

Jacob Samuel Speyer was an Indologist who completed his PhD at Leiden University under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), the University of Groningen (1888–1903), and Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Friedrich Nietzsche and Theodor Benfey at Basel, Göttingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at the University of Basel (1879–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone is a scholar of Japanese religions and Buddhist studies who earned her degrees from San Francisco State University and UCLA under William R. LaFleur. She was a professor at Princeton University from 1990 to 2019.

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed her doctoral studies under Julius Lipner. She has held posts at the University of Manchester, including as an Honorary Research Fellow.

Jacques André was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris. He held academic posts at Aix-Marseille University (1947–1953), the École Pratique des Hautes Études (1953–1978), and Paris Nanterre University (1965–1970).

Jacques Bacot was a Tibetologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Paul Pelliot. He held directorships and lecturing posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études between 1919 and 1938, and served as president of the Société Asiatique.

Jacques Gernet was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at EPHE and INALCO. He held posts at EPHE/EHESS (1955–1976), the University of Paris, Paris Diderot University, and the Collège de France (1975–1992).

Jacques Giès was a scholar of sinology, history, and Buddhist studies who studied at Paris-Sorbonne University under Flora Blanchon. He taught at Paris-Sorbonne and École du Louvre, and served as Chief Curator and President of the Guimet Museum.

Jacques Leider is a historian of Southeast Asia and Buddhist studies. He earned master's degrees from INALCO and Paris-Sorbonne and a PhD under Denise Bernot at INALCO. He taught at Chulalongkorn University and joined the EFEO in 2001.

Jacques May was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate under Constantin Régamey, served as editor-in-chief of Hōbōgirin (~1968–1981), and was a professor at the University of Lausanne (~1974–1990).

Jacques Scheuer was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the Université catholique de Louvain and Sorbonne Nouvelle University under Madeleine Biardeau, and served as a professor at the Université catholique de Louvain from ~1980 to 2007.

Jadunath Sarkar was a historian educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He held teaching posts at Patna College (1899–1926) and Ravenshaw College, served as dean at Banaras Hindu University, and was Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University (1926–1928).
